EVAL_USAGE.title: Arbitrary Code Execution via eval()
EVAL_USAGE.description: The eval() function dynamically executes string inputs as Python code, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary system commands.
EVAL_USAGE.fix:
import ast
# SECURE FIX: Safely evaluate literal structures (strings, numbers, tuples, lists, dicts, booleans, and None) without code execution risk
result = ast.literal_eval(user_input)

COMMAND_INJECTION.title: OS Command Injection via os.system()
COMMAND_INJECTION.description: Passing unconstrained input directly to os.system() allows command chaining through shell metacharacters (e.g., ';', '&&', '|').
COMMAND_INJECTION.fix:
import subprocess
import shlex
# SECURE FIX: Use subprocess.run with argument lists and shell=False to prevent shell parameter parsing
subprocess.run(shlex.split(command), check=True)

HARDCODED_SECRET.title: Use of Hard-coded Sensitive Credentials
HARDCODED_SECRET.description: Hardcoding passwords, API tokens, or encryption keys in source code exposes secrets via revision control systems and compiled assets.
HARDCODED_SECRET.fix:
import os
# SECURE FIX: Retrieve sensitive credentials dynamically from environment variables
API_KEY = os.getenv('API_KEY')
if not API_KEY:
    raise ValueError('Required environment variable API_KEY is missing.')

SQL_INJECTION.title: SQL Injection via String Formatting
SQL_INJECTION.description: Constructing SQL queries using string concatenation or f-strings bypasses query sanitization and enables unauthorized database access.
SQL_INJECTION.fix:
# SECURE FIX: Use parameterized queries to isolate SQL command structure from user parameters
cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ? AND status = ?', (username, 'active'))

INSECURE_DESERIALIZATION.title: Insecure Deserialization via pickle
INSECURE_DESERIALIZATION.description: Deserializing untrusted data with the pickle module can trigger arbitrary code execution during object instantiation.
INSECURE_DESERIALIZATION.fix:
import json
# SECURE FIX: Use safe, standard data serialization formats like JSON instead of Python pickle
data = json.loads(untrusted_payload)

WEAK_CRYPTO.title: Use of Weak Cryptographic Hash (MD5/SHA1)
WEAK_CRYPTO.description: MD5 and SHA-1 algorithms are vulnerable to collision attacks and should not be used for security-critical hashing or password storage.
WEAK_CRYPTO.fix:
import hashlib
# SECURE FIX: Upgrade hash operations to SHA-256 or secure key derivation functions (e.g., Argon2, bcrypt, pbkdf2)
hash_object = hashlib.sha256(data.encode()).hexdigest()

WEAK_RANDOM.title: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Generator
WEAK_RANDOM.description: The standard random module uses the Mersenne Twister engine, which is entirely predictable if outputs are observed.
WEAK_RANDOM.fix:
import secrets
# SECURE FIX: Use the secrets module for security-sensitive operations like token generation
secure_token = secrets.token_hex(32)
